# Deere & Company (NYSE: DE): Strategic Scan, with a Deep Dive on Construction & Forestry

*Figures are the latest available as of early October 2026. Deere's fiscal year ends around 1 November. Fiscal 2025 is the year ended 2 November 2025. Q3 fiscal 2026 is the quarter ended 2 August 2026.*

## Company snapshot

- Deere makes agricultural, turf, construction, forestry and roadbuilding equipment, and it lends money to buyers through its own finance arm (John Deere Financial). It reports four segments: Production & Precision Agriculture, Small Agriculture & Turf, Construction & Forestry, and Financial Services. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- Headquarters: One John Deere Place, Moline, Illinois. The company was incorporated in Delaware in 1958 and has made farm equipment since 1837. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- It is a public company listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DE. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)
- Fiscal 2025 net sales and revenues were $45.684 billion, down 12% from $51.716 billion in fiscal 2024. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)
- Fiscal 2025 net income was $5.027 billion, down from $7.100 billion in fiscal 2024. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)
- Employees: about 73,100 at 2 November 2025, of whom about 27,000 work in the U.S. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- Latest quarter (Q3 FY2026): net sales and revenues were $12.608 billion (up 5%) and net income was $1.379 billion. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)
- Deere expects fiscal 2026 net income of $4.75 billion to $5.00 billion. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)

## Business units

Revenue shares below are my own calculations. Each one is the segment's fiscal 2025 net sales divided by equipment-operations net sales of $38.917 billion. Financial Services is shown separately because it earns financing revenue, not equipment sales.

- **Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA):** large tractors, combines, cotton pickers, sprayers and seeding equipment, plus precision-farming technology. It sells mainly to large commercial farms. Fiscal 2025 net sales were $17.311 billion, about 44% of equipment sales. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm); [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- **Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT):** small and mid-size tractors, hay and forage equipment, and turf and utility equipment. It sells to smaller farms, livestock and dairy producers, landscapers, golf courses and homeowners. Fiscal 2025 net sales were $10.224 billion, about 26% of equipment sales. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm); [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- **Construction & Forestry (CF):** this unit sells four kinds of equipment:
  - construction machines: excavators, motor graders, dozers, wheel loaders, backhoes and articulated dump trucks
  - compact equipment: skid steers and compact track loaders
  - Wirtgen Group roadbuilding equipment: milling, paving, compaction, crushing and asphalt plants
  - forestry machines such as harvesters, forwarders and feller bunchers

  It sells to contractors, rental companies, road builders and forestry businesses through independent dealers and company-owned outlets. Fiscal 2025 net sales were $11.382 billion, about 29% of equipment sales. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf); [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm)
- **Financial Services (John Deere Financial):** retail and wholesale financing, leases and revolving credit for buyers and dealers of Deere equipment. Fiscal 2025 net income was about $1.114 billion. [Deere Q4 FY2025 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm); [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- **Why I scan CF:** you asked for Construction & Forestry. It is the second-largest equipment segment, and it is now the fastest growing. CF net sales for the first nine months of fiscal 2026 rose 26% to $10.079 billion, and operating profit rose 67% to $1.134 billion. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)

## Industries and main competitors

**1. Construction, compact and roadbuilding equipment (CF segment)**

Deere's 10-K names Caterpillar, CNH, Doosan Bobcat, Komatsu, Volvo CE, SANY, XCMG and others as CF competitors. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf) In the KHL Yellow Table 2026 ranking of 2025 construction-equipment sales, Deere is fourth, behind Caterpillar, Komatsu and XCMG. [Construction Briefing – Yellow Table 2026](https://www.constructionbriefing.com/news/yellow-table-2026-worlds-biggest-construction-oems-revealed-/8120453.article)

- **Caterpillar**
  - Strength: much larger scale and higher margins. Its Q2 2026 Construction Industries sales were $8.346 billion (up 35%) at a 23.3% segment margin. Deere CF's Q3 margin was 12.1%. [Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm); [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)
  - Weakness: part of its 2026 profit is one-off. Q2 operating profit included $392 million of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries, which flatters the comparison. Deere also books tariff refunds. [Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm)
- **Komatsu**
  - Strength: global number two, with record revenue in fiscal 2025 and strong mining demand. Deere has little mining exposure. [Powersys – Komatsu record 2025 sales](https://www.powersys.com/2026/05/komatsu-reports-record-2025-sales-but-profits-decline/)
  - Weakness: profits fell. North American residential demand was sluggish, rental-company purchases dropped and costs rose. [Powersys – Komatsu record 2025 sales](https://www.powersys.com/2026/05/komatsu-reports-record-2025-sales-but-profits-decline/)
- **Volvo Construction Equipment**
  - Strength: Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin of 14.4%. It also began delivering serial-produced A30 Electric articulated haulers. [Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)
  - Weakness: reported net sales fell 6%, partly because it sold SDLG. Volvo-brand orders fell in Europe and Asia. [Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)
- **CNH Industrial (Construction)**
  - Strength: Q2 2026 construction sales grew 12% to $866 million, driven by North American shipments. [CNH Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)
  - Weakness: its adjusted EBIT margin was only 1.7%. That is far below Deere CF, and CNH blames tariffs and R&D spending. [CNH Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)

**2. Agricultural and turf equipment (PPA and SAT segments)**

Deere's 10-K names AGCO, CLAAS, CNH Industrial, Kubota and Toro as global competitors. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)

- **CNH Industrial (Case IH, New Holland)**
  - Strength: the second full-line global farm-equipment maker [unverified – not checked against a 2026 source].
  - Weakness: it is much smaller than Deere, with Q2 2026 consolidated revenue of $4.8 billion. [CNH Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001567094/000156709426000015/ex991q226.htm)
- **AGCO (Fendt, Massey Ferguson)**
  - Strength: North American sales grew 19.8% at constant currency in Q2 2026. [Nasdaq – AGCO Q2 2026 release](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/agco-reports-second-quarter-results-2026-07-30)
  - Weakness: its 2026 sales outlook is only $10.1 to $10.2 billion, and its Q2 adjusted operating margin slipped to 6.6% from 8.3%. [AGCO Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000880266/000088026626000066/a2026earningsreleaseq2.htm)
- **Kubota**
  - Strength: strong in compact tractors and compact construction equipment. Its construction-machinery revenue rose 28.6% in Q1 2026 on new model launches. [Equipment World – Kubota Q1 2026](https://www.equipmentworld.com/market-pulse/article/15825607/kubota-reports-strong-start-to-2026-fiscal-year)
  - Weakness: heavily exposed to U.S. tariffs as an importer. Calendar 2025 operating profit fell 15.9%, mainly because of U.S. tariff costs. [Kubota FY2025 financial results](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/136q4e.pdf)

**3. Equipment finance (Financial Services)**

- John Deere Financial mainly finances Deere's own equipment and dealers. It is a support business more than a stand-alone competitor, so I have not analysed its rivals. Its fiscal 2026 net income is forecast at about $870 million. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)

## Environmental scan

PESTLE for **Construction & Forestry only**.

**Political**
- **Tariffs (hurts):** Deere expects about $1.1 billion of direct tariff expense in fiscal 2026 across the company, and a further step-up in fiscal 2027. This raises CF's costs, especially on imported components and Wirtgen machines from Europe. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- **Federal highway funding (uncertain):** the authorities under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act expired on 30 September 2026. Congress signalled that a short extension may be needed while it finishes a new highway bill. Road and bridge work drives demand for Wirtgen and earthmoving equipment, so funding gaps or delays are a risk. [NACo – IIJA authorities expire September 30](https://www.naco.org/news/iija-authorities-expire-september-30-naco-urges-congress-uphold-full-funding-levels-highway)

**Economic**
- **Mixed construction spending (helps big projects, hurts housing):** U.S. construction spending was $2,203.1 billion annualised in August 2026, 1.7% below August 2025. [U.S. Census Bureau – Construction Spending](https://www.census.gov/construction/c30/current/index.html) Deere says infrastructure, data-centre and energy projects are offsetting weak residential building. It expects U.S./Canada construction equipment demand up 5% to 10% and global forestry down about 10%. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
- **Rising interest rates (hurts):** on 16 September 2026 the Fed raised its target range to 3.75%–4.00%, the first increase since 2023. That makes it more expensive for contractors and rental fleets to finance machines. [Atlanta Fed – FOMC statement](https://www.atlantafed.org/news-and-events/2026/09/16/fomc-statement); [CNBC – Fed rate decision September 2026](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html)

**Social**
- **Skilled-labour shortage (helps Deere's technology sales):** 88% of contractors with craft openings say those jobs are as hard or harder to fill than a year ago. Data-centre work is adding to the competition for workers. [AGC – 2026 workforce survey](https://www.agc.org/news/2026/09/03/construction-workforce-shortages-remain-acute-despite-soft-market-conditions-data-centers-strain) This makes Deere's operator-assist and safety technology more useful to customers. Deere sales of jobsite safety solutions are up nearly 40% year over year. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

**Technological**
- **Machine automation (helps):** factory-installed SmartGrade adoption is up more than 50% year to date. Deere has launched three excavator models of its own design, with more to roll out over three to four years. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
- **Electrification (opportunity and race):** in 2023 Deere set a target of more than 20 electric and hybrid construction models by 2026. [Equipment Journal – Deere E-Drive and E-Power at ConExpo](https://www.equipmentjournal.com/construction-equipment/john-deere-electric-excavator-backhoe/) Whether it met that target is [unverified]. Competitors such as Volvo CE are already delivering serial-production electric haulers. [Volvo CE Q2 2026 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-construction-equipment-delivers-increased-volumes-and-improved-earnings-in-q2-2026/)

**Legal**
- **Tariff refunds (helps, one-off):** in February 2026 the Supreme Court ruled that IEEPA does not authorise the President's tariffs, which opened the way to refunds. [Holland & Knight – Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs](https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/02/supreme-court-strikes-down-ieepa-tariffs) Deere has recognised $382 million of tariff refunds so far in fiscal 2026. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)
- **Right to repair (risk of spill-over):** in July 2026 Deere settled the FTC and five-state right-to-repair case. It agreed to give farmers and independent repairers dealer-level repair tools for 10 years. The settlement covers farm equipment only, but construction customers could push for the same access. [FTC press release – Deere settlement](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/07/ftc-states-secure-settlement-deere-company-advancing-farmers-right-repair)

**Environmental**
- **Engine-emissions rules (cost, and a reason to innovate):** the U.S., EU, India and others keep tightening off-road engine-emissions rules. Meeting them requires significant spending on new engines and after-treatment systems, which raises product costs. [Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://investor.deere.com/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf)
- **Forest-products market (hurts forestry):** soft log and lumber prices, plus weak housing, are pulling global forestry equipment demand down about 10% in 2026. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

## Research summary

- **CF is now Deere's growth engine while large agriculture shrinks.** Deere guides CF sales up about 20% and PPA down about 10% for fiscal 2026. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm)
- **CF profit growth is driven by pricing more than volume.** Q3 operating profit rose 84% to $436 million, and Deere credits mainly price realization (8 points of the 18% sales gain). Pricing power that strong may not last if demand cools. [Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm); [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
- **Deere is a profitable number four, not the leader.** Its 10.5%–11.5% CF margin guidance beats CNH but trails Caterpillar's 23.3% construction margin. Deere also slipped behind XCMG in the global ranking. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm); [Construction Briefing – Yellow Table 2026](https://www.constructionbriefing.com/news/yellow-table-2026-worlds-biggest-construction-oems-revealed-/8120453.article)
- **Demand rests on big projects, so policy matters.** Data-centre, energy and infrastructure work is carrying CF while housing is weak. Highway reauthorization and interest rates are therefore the key swing factors. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [NACo – IIJA authorities expire September 30](https://www.naco.org/news/iija-authorities-expire-september-30-naco-urges-congress-uphold-full-funding-levels-highway)
- **Technology is Deere's main way to stand out in a labour-short market.** Grade control and safety systems are growing fast. [Motley Fool – Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

## Suggested further research

- How much of CF's fiscal 2026 operating profit comes from one-off tariff refunds rather than lasting pricing and volume?
- What will the final surface-transportation reauthorization (the successor to the IIJA) provide for highway funding, and when?
- How is Deere's share of U.S. compact construction equipment (skid steers, compact track loaders) moving against Bobcat, Caterpillar and Kubota?
- Did Deere deliver its target of more than 20 electric and hybrid construction models by 2026, and how are they selling?
- Will Chinese makers such as XCMG and SANY become a serious threat in North America, or will tariffs keep them mostly in other regions?

## Limits of this analysis

- Deere is a public company, so its own figures come from audited or SEC-filed sources. No figures here are estimates of private data.
- Revenue shares by segment are my own arithmetic from reported segment sales, not percentages Deere publishes.
- The competitor strength for CNH's farm business is general industry knowledge and is marked [unverified].
- I could not confirm whether Deere met its 2026 electrification target [unverified].
- The Kubota Q1 2026 figures come from a trade-press article whose page I could not open in full. I relied on the search-result summary.
- The AGCO North America growth figure comes from the press release as shown in search results, not from a page I opened.
- Fiscal 2026 is not finished. Full-year numbers are Deere's guidance as of August 2026 and could change when Q4 results come out in November 2026.
- Competitors report on different calendars, so their quarters (for example Caterpillar Q2 to June) do not line up exactly with Deere's Q3 (to 2 August).

## Summary

In fiscal 2025 Deere & Company (NYSE: DE) had $45.7 billion of revenue and $5.0 billion of net income. In fiscal 2026 its Construction & Forestry segment is growing about 20% and lifting margins, while large agriculture declines. CF is the world's fourth-largest construction-equipment business, behind Caterpillar, Komatsu and XCMG. Its demand rests on infrastructure, data-centre and energy projects, and it is exposed to tariffs, highway-funding uncertainty after the IIJA expired and rising interest rates.
